Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Derek Mason succeeding longtime head coach Rick Stockstill and refers to his defensive background.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.oc: Anthony Scelfo, previously at Southeastern Louisiana, where he coached under his father since 2021 — this is his first time calling plays at FBS level.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.dc: Not addressed by name. Derek Mason's own defensive background is the guide's reference point.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.oc_status: New — the guide records Scelfo's arrival, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.play_caller: Anthony Scelfo on offense, in his first FBS play-calling job.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.offensive_scheme: Not named, but its intended direction is stated: the guide's reasoning is scheme plus conference context — Scelfo and a more robust running game with a more mobile quarterback should help, particularly in Conference USA, where teams that run the ball efficiently often fare better.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records 6.7 yards per play allowed in Mason's first year as shocking, then 1.2 yards per carry cut year over year by better players in the front seven, with the secondary continuing to struggle at a tie for 105th nationally in passing plays of 20-plus yards allowed.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.run_pass: Expected to shift toward the run, with the guide concluding that even if the quarterback disappoints, MTSU should run the ball a lot better.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.qb_development: Not addressed as a development record, but the guide raises a pointed structural question about deployment. Under Roman Gagliano the offense scored 26, 31 and 31 points with 541, 460 and 459 yards — figures it says were almost untouchable before Nicholas Vattiato's injury — and he threw for over 1,000 yards with a 7-to-0 ratio. It asks why he was not starting to begin with and answers structurally rather than personally: it does not claim to know the locker-room dynamics, but notes the redshirt freshman was surely earning less NIL money than the programme's all-time second-leading passer, and that some teams — especially at the Group of Six level — seem unwilling to move on from entrenched starters they have invested in.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 6 returning starters, totalling 7.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator, following very minimal offensive improvement.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.prior_school: Southeastern Louisiana for Scelfo, and the connection reaches the roster: Antonio Martin averaged over five yards per carry there in Scelfo's first season as coordinator in 2024. The guide also records Terence Brown from Saginaw Valley State.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.portal_recruiting: Credited as a slow build. The guide extends Mason the benefit of the doubt that after a third portal class and third freshman class he now has players who better fit what he wants defensively, and describes the defense as mostly rebuilt through the portal across two cycles.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.vsin_assessment: A very important year three, with the sharpest criticism aimed at the coach's own specialism. The guide says back-to-back 3-9 seasons inspire little confidence in the programme's direction, and finds the failure most pointed on Mason's own side of the ball: despite his defensive background, MTSU allowed 34.3 points per game in year one and 30.9 in year two, though it credits an improvement of 0.8 yards per play. The thing to build on is late-season gains under Gagliano, who stayed despite opening eyes over the final three games.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.strengths: A returning quarterback whose three starts produced the offense's best figures of the season with a 7-to-0 ratio, a coordinator hire aligned with a run-first plan the guide says suits this conference, a much stronger running back room including a player who already knows the coordinator, defensive-coordinator continuity, a front seven that cut 1.2 yards per carry, and a third portal and freshman class now in place.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.concerns: Back-to-back 3-9 seasons, a defense conceding over 30 points per game under a defensive-minded head coach, a secondary tied for 105th in explosive passes allowed, a first-time FBS play-caller, only six returning starters, and the loss of the leading rusher and every 30-plus-catch receiver but one.
Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Missouri State Bears.previous_hc_experience: None as a head coach. The Coaching Carousel records that Casey Woods has worn a lot of different hats, including offensive coordinator under Rhett Lashlee at SMU and director of player personnel at Auburn, and that he has worked under Gus Malzahn, Bill Clark, Eli Drinkwitz and Lashlee, and is the son of 50-year coaching veteran Sparky Woods. The team pages give his age as 43 and note his father has been a coach since 1976.
Missouri State Bears.oc: Mark Cala, who was Skyler Locklear's quarterbacks coach at UTEP last season.
Missouri State Bears.dc: Jack Curtis, who brings over a decade of experience in the role and was a defensive analyst at Auburn.
Missouri State Bears.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Missouri State Bears.dc_status: New — the guide records Curtis arriving, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Missouri State Bears.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Missouri State Bears.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Missouri State Bears.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's supporting evidence for the hire comes from Auburn, where Curtis was a defensive analyst and Brett Kulka — now Missouri State's defensive ends coach — was assistant defensive line coach on a unit with 30 sacks that held opponents under three yards per carry.
Missouri State Bears.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Missouri State Bears.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide flags one relationship worth watching — Skyler Locklear's quarterbacks coach from last season, Mark Cala, is the new offensive coordinator — and records Duke transfer Henry Belin as having spent four years with the Blue Devils and basically never played.
Missouri State Bears.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 5 returning starters — a total of 0.
Missouri State Bears.staff_turnover: Complete, and the guide explains the mechanism: many players followed head coach Ryan Beard to Coastal Carolina or found homes elsewhere. It adds the roster consequence of the same rule — productive players who wanted to see the FBS transition through then either run out of eligibility or attract better offers.
Missouri State Bears.prior_school: SMU for Woods and for offensive line coach Hussam Ouri, whom the guide identifies as possibly the most important person on that sideline this season. Auburn for both Jack Curtis and defensive ends coach Brett Kulka. UTEP for Mark Cala and Skyler Locklear. The guide also records Henry Belin from Duke.
Missouri State Bears.portal_recruiting: The rebuilding mechanism, and the guide notes returning production is hard to find on the depth chart.
Missouri State Bears.vsin_assessment: A hire the Carousel trusts on the strength of the athletic director, and a year the team pages treat as transitional. The Coaching Carousel says Missouri State had to be quietly planning for Beard to be offered another job but probably did not think it would be so soon, credits AD Patrick Ransdell — who got the job just before the season and understands mid-major football from App State and UCF — with moving quickly, and concludes a man who has worked under Malzahn, Clark, Drinkwitz and Lashlee, and is the son of a 50-year coaching veteran, probably ends up being a solid hire. The team pages combine two unknowns: Woods might turn Belin or Locklear into a quality starter, but there are major questions in the trenches, which is a lot to overlook given the uncertainty at the most important position. They read this as a transitional year after which Woods finds a more suitable quarterback in year two.
Missouri State Bears.strengths: A head coach with an unusually broad background across coordinator, personnel and multiple respected staffs, an offensive coordinator who already coached one of the quarterback candidates, a defensive coordinator with over a decade of experience in the role plus an Auburn position coach who worked with him there, and an athletic director the Carousel considers trustworthy on mid-major hires.
Missouri State Bears.concerns: A Stability Score of 0 with five returning starters, the loss of the programme's all-time second-leading passer and a 1,021-yard rusher, an unproven offensive line on a programme that has allowed 40 or more sacks in five of the last six seasons since 2020 — 52 last year — and a defense that was already conceding 5.9 yards per play.
Missouri State Bears.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
Missouri State Bears.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames the vacancy as expected but early: Missouri State had to be quietly planning for Ryan Beard to be offered another job, but they probably didn't think it would be so soon. With Beard off to Coastal Carolina following the programme's first FBS season, AD Patrick Ransdell — who got the job just before the start of the football season — moved quickly to hire Woods from SMU. Burke lists the breadth of the résumé: Woods has worn a lot of different hats, including OC under Rhett Lashlee and director of player personnel at Auburn. He then vouches for the process rather than only the man — Ransdell understands mid-major football, having worked at App State and UCF previously, so Burke thinks he's trustworthy in isolating Woods as quickly as he did. His conclusion rests on lineage: a man who has worked under Gus Malzahn, Bill Clark, Eli Drinkwitz and Lashlee, and is also the son of 50-year coaching vet Sparky Woods, probably ends up being a solid hire.

New Mexico State Aggies.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide sets Tony Sanchez's seven wins in two seasons against Jerry Kill's 17-11 across 2022 and 2023.
New Mexico State Aggies.oc: David Yost, who has run productive offenses at Texas Tech and Utah State.
New Mexico State Aggies.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
New Mexico State Aggies.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
New Mexico State Aggies.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
New Mexico State Aggies.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
New Mexico State Aggies.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
New Mexico State Aggies.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records the absolute worst rushing offense in the nation at just 77 yards per game, crossing 100 only twice.
New Mexico State Aggies.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Sanchez and Yost having choices — holdover Adam Damante, Furman transfer Trey Hedden with a 30-to-22 ratio but more than 4,700 yards over roughly 20 starts, and Kalani McLeod from Diablo Valley College — and reads Hedden's Division I experience as making him the leader in the clubhouse.
New Mexico State Aggies.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 12.
New Mexico State Aggies.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
New Mexico State Aggies.prior_school: Texas Tech and Utah State for David Yost. On the roster the guide records Trey Hedden from Furman, Kalani McLeod from Diablo Valley College and James Jones from Delaware State.
New Mexico State Aggies.portal_recruiting: Rated middling against a depth problem. 247Sports credits the programme with 26 portal players but ranks the class seventh of the conference's 10 teams, and the guide says depth was a huge issue last season and looks to be again.
New Mexico State Aggies.vsin_assessment: Unfavourable comparison to the predecessor, with the improvement explained away. The guide says Jerry Kill's work in Las Cruces looks more impressive with each passing day and sets his 17-11 against Sanchez's seven wins in two seasons. It admits surprise that New Mexico State improved at all, and explains it by turnovers — from -13 in margin to exactly even as the defense found more takeaways, including nine fumble recoveries. It then argues the defensive gain came down simply to forcing more turnovers, labelling the swing from a single fumble recovery in 2024 to nine in 2025 fumble luck, and notes the underlying pass rush stays weak at 19 sacks last season and only 33 across two seasons.
New Mexico State Aggies.strengths: Full coordinator continuity, an offensive coordinator with productive offenses at two previous Power Four and Group of Five stops, an offensive line the guide says looks most improved with starting experience from the FCS and JUCO ranks, a good number of returning defensive starters and contributors, and a quarterback addition with more than 4,700 career passing yards.
New Mexico State Aggies.concerns: Seven wins in two seasons, the worst rushing offense in the nation, three of the top four pass-catchers gone, a defensive improvement the guide attributes to fumble luck rather than play, a pass rush with 33 sacks in two seasons and both leading rushers of the passer departed, and a portal class ranked seventh of 10.
New Mexico State Aggies.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its projection is 4.61 wins.

Sam Houston State Bearkats.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed as head-coaching experience. The guide describes Phil Longo as a longtime coordinator who likes tempo and the Air Raid.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.oc: Not addressed by name; the guide notes Sam Houston enters 2026 with the same head coach and the same coordinators.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.dc: Freddie Aughtry-Lindsay, in his second year.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator, and the guide notes pointedly that despite the debacle Sam Houston has the same coordinators.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.play_caller: Not addressed by name, but the guide assigns responsibility explicitly: finishing 127th in points per game falls on the players calling out the offense and the person calling it.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.offensive_scheme: Named. The guide identifies Longo as a longtime coordinator who likes tempo and the Air Raid, and uses a mechanical image for the mismatch between scheme and personnel — he is in year two of installing a new system, but is attempting to put a Dodge Dart engine into a Geo Prizm.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records seven yards per play allowed and the worst defense in the nation in yards allowed per game.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.tempo: Stated as a coordinator preference — Longo likes tempo.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.run_pass: Air Raid by design, though the guide defends the run game as serviceable at 4.3 yards per carry, with running backs averaging 5.8, 6.7 and 4.2 and the overall figure dragged down badly by the quarterbacks.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records the quarterbacks combining for a 12-to-10 ratio and just 2,209 yards, and names Landyn Locke the projected starter after throwing for 765 yards at 50.4% completions.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 7 returning starters, totalling 10.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.staff_turnover: None, and the guide flags that as notable in itself: despite the debacle, Sam Houston enters 2026 with the same head coach and the same coordinators.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.prior_school: Temple is where the previous head coach went — the guide records KC Keeler leaving after a 10-3 year in 2024, returning home to southeastern Pennsylvania.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.portal_recruiting: The one clear positive. The guide reports second-year coordinator Freddie Aughtry-Lindsay did a great deal of portal shopping, with 247Sports rating the Bearkats' haul the best in the conference and the secondary a huge focal point.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.vsin_assessment: Unsparing about year one and sceptical about the season that preceded it. The guide records the collapse from 10-3 to 2-10 with year one under Longo not working out at all — the offense terrible, the defense worse — and stresses the underlying numbers despite a +2 turnover margin: out-scored by 20 points per game overall and 19 in conference play, with seven yards per play allowed, figures it calls extremely difficult to build off. It forecloses the schedule excuse directly, noting the Bearkats gave up more yards per game to conference opponents in a terrible offensive conference, and says a dearth of talent is one thing but the numbers do not inspire confidence in the play-caller either. It then reopens the 10-3 season and finds it thinner than it looked — 23.8 points scored against 20.5 allowed, +0.2 in yards per play, a +12 turnover margin doing a lot of heavy lifting, a -2 sack differential and a 6-0 record in one-possession games — concluding it is hard not to see 2023 and 2025 as more representative.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.strengths: Full staff continuity into year two of the system, a roster the guide says may be closer to what the head coach wants, a serviceable run game once quarterback carries are excluded, and the best-rated portal haul in the conference with the secondary a focal point.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.concerns: A 2-10 season out-scored by 20 points per game with seven yards per play allowed, the worst defense in the nation in yards per game, a scheme-personnel mismatch the guide describes in blunt terms, a projected starting quarterback who completed 50.4% of his passes, and a coordinator staff retained despite the results.
Sam Houston State Bearkats.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its projection is 2.66 wins.

Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide characterises Tyson Helton by his floor — at least eight wins in six of seven seasons, nine games four times, and only one missed bowl, which it says can probably be blamed on COVID.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.oc: Bodie Reeder, who has run some pretty potent passing offenses, replacing Rick Bowie, who was one-and-done after arriving from Abilene Christian with quarterback Maverick McIvor.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.dc: Davis Merritt, on staff for three years.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.oc_status: New — the guide records Bowie's single season and Reeder's arrival, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.offensive_scheme: Not named, but characterised by the coordinator's history: Reeder has run some pretty potent passing offenses and the guide judges him a better fit here than at his previous stop at Middle Tennessee.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide notes a rotation effect — only three players had 70-plus tackles because Western Kentucky rotated heavily to stay fresh — and records 19 sacks against 22.6 points allowed, the fewest since 2019.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide's conditional is that if Rodney Tisdale can distribute the ball without turning it over and prove more of a running threat, the unit will be cooking with gas quickly.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide judges Tisdale contextually — just under 66% completions with a 9-to-7 ratio and 2.1 yards per carry is not great, but he was a true freshman, and although he must learn a new playbook he is the most dynamic option on the roster — and notes Florida State transfer Brock Glenn has a chance if he falters or is hurt.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 0 for 7 returning starters, totalling 11.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.staff_turnover: Identified as the programme's one unstable position. The guide's premise is that virtually every programme is in constant motion and that some nonetheless look more stable than others — Western Kentucky being one — with the offensive coordinator position the variable that has not been constant.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.prior_school: Middle Tennessee for Bodie Reeder, and Abilene Christian for the departed Rick Bowie and Maverick McIvor. On the roster the guide records Ajay Allen from Tulsa, Zion Taylor from Georgia Tech, Jyzaiah Rockwell from the FCS ranks and an Alabama transfer on the offensive line.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.portal_recruiting: Used to rebuild the trenches and the skill positions. The guide singles out the offensive line as a genuine upgrade — a hodgepodge of transfers, but with a lot more experience and size than last season's group.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.vsin_assessment: Stability as the defining characteristic, with one variable isolated. The guide characterises the programme by its floor rather than its ceiling under Helton, identifies the offensive coordinator position as the thing that has not been constant, and rates Reeder a better fit here than at Middle Tennessee. Its conditional forecast is that if Reeder can get Western Kentucky back over 30 points per game, consistent defensive play would leave the Hilltoppers poised for their first conference title since 2016. On the defense its stated conclusion is pessimism, resting on the run defense needing fixing, the low sack totals, and complete turnover in the front seven.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.strengths: A head coach with at least eight wins in six of seven seasons and only one missed bowl, a coordinator hire the guide considers a better fit than at his last stop, a returning quarterback the guide calls the most dynamic option, defensive-coordinator continuity with a system ingrained over three years, backups already familiar with the scheme thanks to heavy rotation, and an offensive line upgraded through the portal.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.concerns: A third different offensive coordinator arrangement in as many seasons, only one returnee of consequence at the skill positions, only two returning defensive contributors, 19 sacks generated, and complete turnover in the front seven.
Western Kentucky Hilltoppers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its coaching-linked conditional is that Reeder returning the offense to 30 points per game would put Western Kentucky in position for a first conference title since 2016.
